newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine prime minister Lazarenko resigns - aide.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine prime minister Lazarenko resigns - aide.

text.p: Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko tendered his resignation on Tuesday and expected President Leonid Kuchma to accept it, an aide said on Tuesday.
This appeared to end uncertainty over the fate of the prime minister, who was temporarily replaced last month in a move which his aides said was a ploy to get rid of him.

Kuchma has come under increasing pressure from Western and Ukrainian officials to dismiss Lazarenko, 44, whose links to the lucrative energy sector have been the subject of widespread speculation in Ukraine and the West.

"The prime minister called a meeting with his close aides and he told us he had offered his resignation to the president," the aide, who asked not to be named, told Reuters, adding: "He was sure the president would accept it."
The aide said Lazarenko, who was replaced by his deputy "for the time of his illness" and taken to hospital on June 19, did not give an official reason for his resignation.
"We were not told about the official reason and also were told not to comment on his resignation," the aide said.

Kuchma's office said no decree had yet been issued on the subject. But a source closed to Kuchma told Reuters that it was likely that president would sign a decree accepting Lazarenko's resignation on Wednesday.
There were varying accounts on what was wrong with Lazarenko when he was taken into hospital last month.
Western media have said that he was behind Ukraine's biggest gas trader, the United Energy Systems of Ukraine, and received $200 million in revenues.
Lazarenko was the initiator and backer of a scheme introduced in 1995 which involved private companies distrubuting gas on the Ukrainian market. He denies any personal gain.
